axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps Notion workspace capabilities
(search, page read/write, database queries) as tools for agents.
axes.runtime:
Official hosted remote server (endpoint mcp.notion.com/mcp — direct fetch 401 = exists but needs auth, not a dead link);
no official docs for a local form. notion.mcp.run direct-fetched 000 (noted as network-restricted).
axes.local_files: Never touches the local file system — the scope is the Notion cloud workspace (pages, databases, comments).
axes.background: The service is resident on Notion's side; MCP sessions are request-response, no background-task semantics.
axes.tools:
Search, fetch pages, create/edit pages and database entries, etc.; the complete tool inventory follows the official docs, not enumerated item by item.
Write capabilities exist (create pages/edit blocks); the boundary follows workspace sharing and permissions.
axes.context: No server-side cross-session memory — state lives in the Notion workspace itself; the Notion AI memory line is a separate product and does not count as this one.
axes.permissions:
OAuth user auth + the workspace permission model: what the agent can see/change follows the page-sharing permissions of the connected Notion account —
this is the selection key: whose account you connect = whose visibility.
axes.fit:
Fits: agents reading and writing the team knowledge base, writing meeting notes/tasks into Notion databases, retrieving context from the wiki.
Not a fit: offline/self-hosted needs (no local form); tool-level isolation finer than account permissions.

mcp.transport:
**Streamable HTTP remote hosting** (mcp.notion.com/mcp); no official docs for a local stdio form.
Verified: official docs page 200, endpoint 401 (direct fetch 2026-10-21).
mcp.auth:
OAuth browser authorization flow (log into the Notion account on first connection); no official docs for a plaintext-token configuration route.
Workspace admins can control connections (admin-approval surface details not verified item by item).
mcp.scope:
Scope = the connected account's workspace visibility; both read and write (search/fetch pages/create pages/edit blocks).
No official docs seen for a tool-level approval mechanism — tightening the write surface relies on account permissions and client-side confirmation.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The complete tool inventory (not enumerated item by item)
- The granularity of workspace-admin control over MCP connections (not verified item by item)
- Rate-limit details (official docs give no numbers)
related: Both official remote servers for collaboration SaaS: the Slack version has a heavier admin-approval surface, the Notion version's write surface is more direct.
sources: Notion · official MCP docs (endpoint and auth wording, direct-fetched and verified 2026-10-21)
